family: War and emergency orders (First World War measures, Alien Property Custodian sales, eight-hour suspensions, one air-space reservation)

mechanisms.description: An order whose only command revokes, rescinds, amends, restores, dissolves a body created by another order, declares another order's authorization terminated, or itself takes title, does all it commands on issue; its effect is evidence for the other order's lifecycle.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The order's date (an order that states a later effective hour is spent at that hour).

mechanisms.description: An order that states its own end: a fixed day (EO 3233, EO 6023), the duration of the war (EO 2652), or the war plus six months after a treaty of peace is proclaimed (EO 2929).
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The stated day, read inclusively; for war-keyed terms, no later than the proclamation of the last 1921 peace treaty (Dec. 20, 1921) or six months after it (June 20, 1922).

mechanisms.description: EO 3320 terminated and abolished the Food Administration and the office of Wheat Director and confined the Grain Corporation to liquidation, ending the orders that created or staffed those offices or directed their operations.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Aug. 21, 1920 (fixed for orders the abolition names; for the others, no later than that day).

mechanisms.description: EO 3154 ended the Committee on Public Information, and with it the orders creating the Committee and its divisions.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Aug. 21, 1919, the date NARA records for the abolition.

mechanisms.description: The Lever Act's provisions ceased to be in effect when the war with Germany terminated, which S1 fixes as March 3, 1921 (the Lever Act is not among S1's exceptions). Orders whose only operation is to vest, delegate or direct the exercise of Lever Act powers had nothing left to operate on.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: No later than March 3, 1921 (interval from the order's date).

mechanisms.description: The Overman Act's termination paragraph restored every agency's statutory functions 'any authorization of the President under this Act to the contrary notwithstanding', so its ending reached the orders made under it.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Between Sept. 3, 1921 (six months after March 3, 1921 under S1) and June 20, 1922 (six months after the last treaty proclamation); claimed as an interval from the order's date to June 20, 1922.

mechanisms.description: The emergency shipping fund section ended all authority granted to the President by it 'or by him delegated' six months after the final treaty of peace with Germany was proclaimed.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: No later than May 14, 1922 (six months after Nov. 14, 1921); Sept. 3, 1921 if S1 is read to govern that clause.

mechanisms.description: EO 3019-A dissolved the War Industries Board on Jan. 1, 1919 except for winding-up and listed functions, all resting on Overman Act authority that ended with that Act (M6).

mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The revoking order's date (Sept. 6, 1918 for EO 2952); EO 3180 operates as of July 14, 1919 though issued Nov. 25, 1919.

mechanisms.description: The War Trade Board's functions were transferred to the State Department and the Board abolished effective June 30, 1919 under EOs 3059 and 3086-A; that performance exhausted the transfer orders and ended appointments to the Board.

S1 fixes March 3, 1921 as the end of the war for Acts, joint resolutions and proclamations contingent on it. It ends no order by itself: it reaches an order only through the statute the order rests on, does not govern an executive order's own words such as 'during the war', and excepts the Trading with the Enemy Act.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: March 3, 1921, only through a statute that by its terms depends on the war's end.

mechanisms.description: Alien Property Custodian functions were transferred (EO 6694 of 1934 to the Department of Justice; EO 9095 of 1942 to a new Custodian; EO 9788 of 1946 to the Attorney General; the Office of Alien Property was abolished in 1966 with blocking controls moved to Treasury by EO 11281). A transfer of functions carries an authorization forward; none of these instruments, nor the Knox-Porter Resolution's sec. 5, extinguishes a First World War sale authorization.

An order authorizing the Custodian (or Frank L. Polk as delegate) to sell, reject bids for, resell or release named property is exhausted when that act is done; the order sets no deadline, so whether and when it was done must come from the Custodian's reports.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The date of sale, rejection or release, from the Custodian's reports (not held).

mechanisms.description: An eight-hour suspension for named work or contracts ends when that work is completed, on a stated term, or by a further order; the suspension authority itself (39 Stat. 1192) is not war-contingent.

41 Stat. 1359 governs Acts, joint resolutions and proclamations, not an executive order's own words, so March 3, 1921 is not used as the date.

procedure.description: Alien Property Custodian sale, rejection-of-bids, resale and release determinations (including Frank L. Polk's orders under EO 3016): single authorizations exhausted only when the act was done.

lead.basis: The order authorizes (or directs) one disposition of named property under sec. 12 of the Trading with the Enemy Act and sets no deadline. It is spent when the sale, rejection, resale or release is made, but no held record shows that it was made. The Trading with the Enemy Act is excepted from the 1921 resolution and is still law, and the later transfers of the Custodian's functions (EO 6694, 9095, 9788; the 1966 abolition of the Office of Alien Property) moved the functions without extinguishing authorizations, so no class event ends an unexercised authorization.

gaps: The Custodian's report for 1918 to Feb. 15, 1919 and the annual reports for 1919-1934 (S17) would show the sale or rejection for each trust; until one is held the order stays open.
Property returned under the Settlement of War Claims Act of 1928 (45 Stat. 254; not held) would make an unexercised authorization moot; that would need its own evidence.
Orders covering several lots or properties need one end per lot.
EO 2832 is a general rule (private sale of merchandise in lots worth no more than $10,000), not a single authorization; it ends only by revocation or supersession, which is not held.

procedure.description: Other orders under the Trading with the Enemy Act: delegations of powers to the Custodian, the Treasury, the Attorney General and the War Trade Board, and general rules.

lead.basis: The Trading with the Enemy Act is excepted from the 1921 resolution and remains in force; the order's delegations were carried forward by later transfers rather than ended, and no held instrument revokes it.

gaps: A revocation or supersession of each delegation (for example by EO 6694 of 1934, EO 9095 of 1942 or later delegations under sec. 5(b)) must be found and read; EO 6694's text is not held. EO 2729-A is a multi-part order whose Censorship Board part was ended by EO 3132 and whose War Trade Board part ended with the Board (B11-B12); its other parts remain open.

procedure.description: Eight-hour-law suspensions or waivers for named work, contracts or agencies.

lead.basis: Each order suspends the eight-hour law for named construction, contracts or purchase orders (EO 2656, 2663, 2678, 2769), for an agency's contracts 'during the present national emergency' (EO 2864, 2928), or for Shipping Board repair contracts 'until further order' (EO 3015). The authority (39 Stat. 1192, or sec. 2 of the Act of June 19, 1912) is not contingent on the 1917 war, so the 1921 resolution does not reach it; completion of the work, or the end of the 'present national emergency' an executive order speaks of, is not recorded.

gaps: Completion records for the Post Office equipment shops (Washington), the Treasury buildings at 500-508 Fourteenth Street NW, the Alaska Railroad car contracts and the D.C. fuel yards; a revoking order for EO 3015; an instrument fixing the end of the 'present national emergency' for EOs 2864 and 2928.

procedure.description: Single acts and transfers whose performance is not recorded: seizure or transfer of named vessels, piers and transports, appraisal boards, transfers of records, property and funds, disposal of materials, and the CPI transfer itself.

lead.basis: The order commands a single act (take over a vessel, transfer piers, ships, records or funds, appoint an appraisal board) or a continuing custody arrangement; it is spent only when performed, and no held record shows performance and its date.

gaps: Shipping Board and Navy annual reports (vessels, piers, transports), NARA administrative histories (records transfers), and the Housing Corporation's reports (EO 2912, 2952, 3296) would show performance. EO 2859-A has no held text.

procedure.description: Catch-all: agencies and government corporations that continued under later liquidation (Grain Corporation EO 2681 and 3320; U.S. Housing Corporation EO 2985-A, 3408), radio and cable control (2585, 2605-A, 2604), the consular-fee order 'during the continuance of the war and until further orders' (2826), and other continuing war orders (2616, 2645, 2687, 2874, 2888, 3017, 3053-A).

lead.basis: No ending basis that reaches the order is held: its authority is not shown to have ended with a statute that reached it, or it created a body whose dissolution date is not held, or its own term is ambiguous.

gaps: Grain Corporation and Housing Corporation dissolution records; the return of radio stations and the end of cable censorship; the naval emergency fund's and the Act of July 18, 1918's own termination clauses (EO 2687, 3017); the Act of Apr. 22, 1918's text (EO 2888, which may fall under B14); reading of EO 2826's 'and until further orders'.

undecidable.reason: Alien Property Custodian authorizations to sell, reject bids, resell or release: whether and when each act was done is in the Custodian's reports, not held (148 members).
Trading with the Enemy Act delegations and general rules: the Act is excepted from the 1921 resolution and still in force; supersession of each delegation not yet read.
Eight-hour suspensions: completion of the work, or the end of an executive order's 'present national emergency', not recorded.
Single acts and transfers whose performance is not recorded.
Bodies continued in liquidation, communications control, ambiguous own terms, statutes whose termination clause is not yet read.
Misclassified members and a text conflict.
